tasks.short: Follow discharged patients and assess treatment effectiveness

steps.what: Review discharged patients due for follow-up and their treatment context
Contact discharged patients to follow their progress and current circumstances
Write and check the reported progress in the existing follow-up note

loop.purpose: Draft the existing progress note from the counselor's explicit dictation
loop.input: Counselor's dictated account of the follow-up contact for the identified patient
loop.output: Draft progress note with attribution and uncertainties
loop.check: Counselor checks patient identity, dates, reported progress and every risk statement against the contact account
loop.stop: One correction; missing or uncertain statements are manually entered and unsupported content removed
loop.why_not_simpler: Follow-up narratives vary beyond fixed fields

steps.what: Determine what follow-up progress indicates about treatment effectiveness
Write the effectiveness judgement and limitations in the current case record

tasks.design: Use a native due-follow-up view in {OTHER}, the care-record application, and bounded dictation drafting for the existing contact note. The counselor contacts the patient, interprets treatment effectiveness and separately writes that judgement in the case record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Due-case navigation and repeated note assembly consume follow-up time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native case views and care-record dictation can assist these operations without deciding effectiveness automatically.
tasks.still_hard: Non-response, self-report limits and changing life circumstances weaken causal conclusions.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the person's progress without attributing every change to the treatment.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated follow-up handling while retaining contact and clinical interpretation.

reach.learn: Distinguish absence of follow-up data from successful treatment

evidence.claim: Attendi describes dictation into care-record reports, including GGZ use; local follow-up savings remain unmeasured.
The Hengelo summarisation pilot retained workers' own notes and achieved little saving, so duplicate capture must be counted.

assumptions: The progress note and effectiveness assessment are existing case records used by the counselor and care team. No new outcome survey, population report or follow-up alert is introduced.

The counselor reads discharge date, planned follow-up date and contact details in s1 and verifies contact identity in s2. The existing follow-up plan is maintained as part of current case handling, with no newly imposed capture contract. Missing dates require manual case review.

The counselor produces progress facts in s2 and dictates them in s3; dictation and verification stay inside the 14 retained note hours. The loop never invents patient outcomes or treatment effectiveness.

The due view removes 4.5 of 15 case-navigation hours; stable assessment headings remove 1 of 10 writing hours. No automatic patient reminder or second-system write-back is implied. Ordinary same-system author saves have no self-gate.
research_questions: Does the due view and drafted note reduce total work after manual fallback, non-response and quality checks?

already_counted.description: Dictate and verify follow-up progress and write the actual effectiveness judgement

incremental.description: Check changed drafting behaviour and maintain the due-case view

approvals.approved_version: Verified patient recipient and exact follow-up questions and disclosures on the current contact; recipient or content changes require reconsideration

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 central B=100, R=88.5, gross 11.5 less 2 upkeep gives 9.5 net. Conservative case: missing due-date metadata retains all 15 navigation hours, duplicate capture and correction retain 18 note hours and all 10 assessment-writing hours; other 55 and 2 upkeep give zero. Usable due metadata retaining 12 navigation hours and bounded drafting retaining 16 note hours, with 9 assessment-writing hours plus other 55 and 2 upkeep, gives 6 net. Patient contact and effectiveness judgement remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with families about treatment planning and progress

steps.what: Review current treatment planning, progress and permitted family disclosure
Confer with family members about treatment plans and progress
Write the family discussion and unresolved concerns in the existing case note

tasks.design: Use a native treatment-plan view and existing family-contact note headings in {OTHER}, the care-record system. The counselor retains the family conversation and separately writes the actual case note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated record navigation and contact-note structure consume a small share of family communication work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views and note headings can remove these operations without generating personal treatment advice.
tasks.still_hard: Relationships, disagreement and disclosure limitations require responsive judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Explain progress appropriately and understand the family's concerns without overriding the client.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated record handling while preserving family engagement.

reach.learn: Keep disclosed information and remaining questions explicit

evidence.claim: Native treatment views and contact-note headings can reduce navigation and repeated structure; local effects are E1 assumptions.

assumptions: The family-discussion note already informs subsequent care-team contact. No new family letter, transcript or communication log is added.

The counselor checks current plan, family identity and disclosure scope in s1-s2 and captures discussed facts and unresolved questions in s3, with capture counted. Missing permission or uncertain identity stops disclosure and is resolved manually.
The native view removes 1.5 of 15 navigation hours. Stable contact headings and identity fields remove 3 of 20 writing hours; the remaining 17 contain actual discussion content and verification.
Ordinary same-system author saves remain retained and have no self-approval gate. No automatic family message, recording or second-system transfer is implied.
research_questions: Does native reuse remove the specified repeated actions while retaining all family-specific content and disclosure checks?

already_counted.description: Write and check the actual family-discussion note

incremental.description: Maintain the native contact-note view when fields change

approvals.approved_version: Exact information and treatment explanation disclosed to the verified permitted family member; new recipients, permissions or content require reconsideration

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 central B=100, R=95.5, gross 4.5 less 0.5 upkeep gives 4 net. Conservative case: permissions require full manual navigation and current headings leave only half an hour removable, offset by half an hour upkeep. Compatible record metadata removing one lookup hour and reusable contact headings removing two writing hours retain 97 hours and 0.5 upkeep gives 2.5 net. Family conversation remains fully retained in both cases.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain direct follow-up and family relationships while reducing repeated case-record handling.
reach: Connect post-discharge progress with qualified treatment evaluation
Keep family communication aligned with the client's permitted disclosure scope
skills_to_grow: Check dictated notes for attribution and invented risk content
Use native follow-up views without hiding capture effort
Separate conversations from actual case writing
role.ambitious_version: A counselor with clear follow-up records and more reliable family communication while personally judging treatment progress.
